title: How Are Plants Classified? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
A moss on the wall, a fern in a pot, a pine on a hill and a mango tree: all four are plants, but are they the same kind? Diya walks through the college garden and asks who decides which plants belong together, and how. This lesson opens Chapter 3, Plant Kingdom, of NCERT Class 11 Biology.

You will see what the plant kingdom holds today and the three ways botanists have sorted plants: the artificial system (a few features, like Linnaeus and the androecium), natural systems (many features outside and inside, Bentham and Hooker) and phylogenetic systems (a family tree with a common ancestor). A labelled flower and a labelled stem section show the features each system uses, and a live key sorts moss, fern, pine and mango one question at a time. We also meet the new tools: numerical taxonomy, cytotaxonomy and chemotaxonomy. Then a worked example, the exam trap about numerical taxonomy, an original NEET pattern match the following question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 21 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
